newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Afghan militia said to close Kashmiri camps.
newsitem.headline: Afghan militia said to close Kashmiri camps.

text.p: A rightist political party in Pakistan-ruled Kashmir said on Saturday the Taleban Islamic militia had closed camps in Afghanistan that trained Kashmiri militants fighting Indian rule in the rest of the Himalayan region.

Abdul Rashid Turabi, chief of the state's Jamaat-i-Islami party, told reporters in Muzaffarabad, capital of Pakistan-held Azad (free) Kashmir, that the camps were closed after Taleban captured Khost province in eastern Afghanistan this month.

There was no confirmation from Taleban, which seized the capital Kabul from the forces of ousted president Burhanuddin Rabbani on Friday after sweeping through vast areas of the east of the country earlier this month.
Turabi said his party set up two camps at Khost in early 1989 to give military training to militants fighting Indian rule over two-thirds of Kashmir. Pakistan rules the remaining third.

He accused Taleban of arresting more than 100 people at the camps in a move which he said also involved Pakistani intelligence agencies. "It was an international conspiracy to sabotage Kashmir's liberation movement," he said.
Pakistan denies Indian charges that it arms and trains the militants who launched an insurgency in India's Jammu and Kashmir state, saying its support for them is only moral and political.
Police and hospitals say more than 20,000 people have been killed since the present revolt erupted there in January 1990.
